notes.title: Small Patch 1.1.1
notes.notes:
This is a small update today, mainly to fix a few bugs and QOL issues reported by players.  So lets get right to it!

-  There was a soft lock bug with splitting cards when you don't have a legacy card.  This effected many players in the prologue, who found the game soft locked after splitting a card.  This issue should now be resolved.

-Fixed an issue with negative choices remaining in the various offerings and a soft lock bug related to this.

- Some players reported that they lost a great legacy card because they entered the next run too quickly and were stuck with playing the Scholar instead of playing the last character.  Now, when returning to the Character Select menu, it will default to the last played character instead of the Scholar.

-Added new combat music for the bounty enemy fight.  Neil Quillen did a fantastic job with this new music track!  You should hear it when you are fighting the last enemy in a bounty.

-Fixed a minor issue with text overlapping on some cards in the Credits screen.

That's all for today.  Be on the lookout for the next update coming soon!

notes.title: Prologue map node visual update
notes.notes: Minor visual update to the map nodes in the prologue, which were off screen in the prologue because of a bug related to the challenge mode update.

notes.title: Update for split swap cards
notes.notes:
One more launch update for today.  This one is super minor and most of you probably won't even notice the change, but it's important to us that we address the feedback we get from you, our players.  Know that we read all of the feedback that you send us.  We appreciate all of your support!

- Fixed a bug with swapping a split card.  Our formula for comparing cards had some trouble when it came to cards that were split.  As a result, half of the time when you swap a card that was split, it would swap the wrong one.  But this has now been resolved and cards should be swapped correctly.
- Fixed a minor bug with the archive view.  When  you open the archive view during a run, it will default to the tab of your current archetype.  However, if you clicked on the Scholar's tab, nothing would happen.  This has been resolved and you will see the Scholar cards update now.
- There were a few other bug fixes around the visualization of the map nodes.

That's it for now.  I hope you all are enjoying the game!  Keep the feedback coming!
-Your friendly neighborhood programmer, Reggi, the Meticulous

notes.title: Performance Hotfix
notes.notes:
Hey all! We’ve got another small patch for you today. Here’s the list:

Art Updates!
Several Background environments saw improvement with the biggest glow ups being the Mountain and Underwater scenes. Check um out!
Character Icons were updated
A smattering of cards received new art, with more to come before 1.0!
Performance Improvements!
This change aims to resolve issues with large deck sizes. We want to stop the game from slowing down when you add 100 Blades to your awesome blade deck. 
The Character Select Screen now highlights the Player Ability.
The UI for Player vs. Enemy cards in the deck was improved to better correlate those numbers to the deck.
Some Trickster cards were balanced to encourage play while in the Lucky Seven state.

We’re deeply excited to come into a 1.0 version of Mori Carta in just a few short days. Looking forward to sharing it with you all!

notes.title: Bounty System Update
notes.notes:
Hey there all you Mori Cartians! We’re back with another update. To be honest, we have been a little quiet on the update front because we’ve got some exciting news:

Mori Carta will be leaving Early Access on March 25th!

That’s right! In just 10 short days we will be putting our best foot forward with a release into 1.0. We wanted to update you with a sneak peak of what’s to come. Let’s get started talking about this patch!

New Features:

Bounty System: We felt that the previous system with the map was fine, but it lacked a sense of cohesion with the rest of the game.  We listened to our players and decided that we wanted a system that felt more like the offerings.  So we created something that we believe suits the design of Mori Carta better than the previous system, and provides more information to the player so they can make strategic decisions.  Players can now choose several ‘bounty’ encounters during their run.  This allows players to fight new enemies they haven’t seen before or face off against enemies that are better suited for the player’s style/deck.
Players receive unique rewards based on the bounty chosen.
We’ve set up a tutorial to show how bounties work.
Sacrifice functionality has been reintroduced via one of the companions.

Gameplay Enhancements:

Card Changes
Many cards were changed, included is a list of some more notable alterations:
Scholar
Forbidden Offer now exhausts.
Trickster:
Boar’s Breath now adds 2 energy in addition to the 3 might. When at 7 energy the card will now fully refund its cost.
Cover your tracks now costs 0 on each side and was moved down to rare from epic.
Dance of daggers now costs 6 and adds 3 energy in addition to the 2 riposte. When at 7 energy the card will now fully refund its cost.
Insecurities reduced to 8 damage from 10
Jagged Bag name changed to “Tools of the Trade” and it’s left side replaced with add 3 Arrows and exhaust.
Killing time was raised to epic rarity and given a significant power increase
7 of sovereignty now exhausts on the right side and reduces enemy might by 3.
Trophy case now costs 4, doesn’t exhaust, and gives 2 energy in addition to the 3 might on reshuffle. When at 7 energy the card will now fully refund its cost.
Druid
Loamwood’s call name changed to “Peace Pipe” and add card was replaced with gain block equal to resilience.
Lick the wounds and Tears had their sides flip to enable healing to be resonated more easily with Hearth Hewn.
Sol and Lun had their downgrade “Eclipse” changed to enable better resonating.
Sow now adds random archetype cards.
Wendigo spirits is now quick. It also exhausts and duplicates on the left side.
Atoned
Profligates changed from 3 damage or 3 block to 5 damage or 5 block. Since Profligates are added by many cards, this change is wide sweeping.
Companions
Rael has had the Wound on his wheel replaced by Duplicate.
Artwork
More art added to card faces
Card back art (boss card, dialogue card, etc.) added to distinguish more specific card types.
New art added for enemies and enemy cards
Art added for legacy cards and enemies
Cards in the shop fan out and look more dynamic
Music
A new music track has been added for battles!
Archive View
Archive view can now be accessed from the pause menu.  This means players can look through their unlocked cards at any time in the game
Quest and Curse tabs were added to the archive view for viewing those cards
Enemy card locking/unlocking was added and now works properly.  This does mean that all the enemies will appear locked now until you encounter them.
Achievements
New achievements were added and content was created for them.

Bug Fixes:

Fixed bug with safe shuffle where not having quick cards would cause the same cards to appear on top every time.
Sorting issues with scholar shops fixed.
Lesser enemy rewards now have a choice on both left and right sides.
Fixed some echo rewards that didn't upgrade the legacy card but instead added the new legacy card.

Miscellaneous:

Fonts have been updated in game to be more eye catching and consistent
There are now distinct fonts for cards and UI elements
Loading Screen is now faster and has been updated with new loading animation
Tooltip updates to address potential sizing issues
Added more secrets.  

We appreciate the support we have received over our Early Access. Thank you for playing our game in its early stages. We can’t wait to hear from fans old and new as we enter the next phase for Mori Carta. It’ll only get better from here.

notes.title: Quest Update
notes.notes:
Hey all!

We got another patch for you! There are bug fixes, card changes, features and more! Check it out and let us know what you think by replying here on Steam or in our Discord!

We’ve got a new feature: Quests! We’re bringing in a first pass at this new map node type to let players have a bit more options in their routing. This also helps to address an oddity that we were noticing with rewards and healing. 

Quests are another way to find healing and other rewards during your run! Where healing rewards felt like they were often a necessity, Quests are an added complication in a fight with a sweet, sweet reward at the end! They are in a very early state, so who knows where exactly quests will land. But we anticipate this to be a good change in favor of the player!

Some other features in no particular order:

A new card effect was added, Permanently Add.  This effect is currently only found on quest cards.  Some quests will allow you to add cards permanently to your deck, the same way that cards in the offerings do.
The Archetype images on character select now have an animation on them!
Lots of new art on cards. Let us know your favorite!
If a card adds more than one card, you can now see both of them in the detail view!
There are a couple new songs in the general offering and cursed offering screens! Look for more to come in the future.
Fixed a bug with some trigger effects that weren't working properly.


Class Card Changes:
Trickster:

With a few exceptions, we have shifted cards that add either blades, arrows, or moss pills to slow by default! This had some pretty interesting implications for some of the builds in Trickster, so let us know what kind of builds you can cook up!
Cloak of Shadows has been changed to mirror Mirror Blade! Pay one to duplicate on the right or exhaust on the left to dodge.
Distract has been fully redesigned. It now gives negative might and negative enemy might. So if you have more attack symbols than wound symbols in your deck, this could be a powerful card!
Friends in Low Places has been rebalanced. It can help you set up for 7 one time, or be reused to add some blades at a cost. Instead of gambling on one or the other.
Gamble now discards cards equal to X instead of adding a debt to do that next turn.
Maximum Effort has been changed as well! It now adds 5 Efforts, but they also add enemy might. Why would we do that? Let’s see if our deck builders and theory crafters can find out!
Untouchable has gained new functionality as an enemy might epic. Every time they hit you, it will hurt less!


Druid:

Cloven Drum had its effect flipped to the left side and its cost reduced. This will make it harder on average to resonate, but easier to play.
Proliferate, Sporecrawl Shield, Tribal Rite, and Roe’s Resolve have all been made default quick! These cards were asking a lot of the player to make the dream happen. We’re gonna try to make that dream easier for you. In my testing, it seems a bit strong, but let’s see what silly stuff you can do with it before we nerf it!
There are a slew of cards that have been redesigned. Mountains Move is a good example! It can now be shifted to the other side through an upgrade downgrade. While Cards like Winter Coat alternate to a different effect entirely. Check it out!

notes.title: The Mighty Update
notes.notes:
In our continued effort to make the game more fair and interesting, we proudly present a new card effect, Enemy Might!  Enemy might will allow us to create both friendly and enemy cards that increase the stakes of a fight without directly hitting you.  We intend to do a lot more with this effect, but for now we made some new enemies and modified some friendly cards.  We also did a pass on many friendly cards, mostly on the Trickster, in an effort to balance the game.  Here is a short list of some of the changes in this update.

-  Enemy Might added to the pool of card effects!
-  Many cards on the Trickster that add cards were made slow.

Arrow Traps
Big Bag
Bottomless Bag
Distract
Jagged Bag
Mossy Distillation
Stockpile III
Trifold


-  Several Trickster cards received negative enemy might as an alternative defensive option to dodge and riposte

Ridicule
Sapping Shiv
Sapping Strike
Serpent Shade
Twist the Blade


-  6 new enemies were created that use enemy might
-  Anara's companion quest has 2 new enemies added to it and was rebalanced
-  To The Brink, a high stakes card, was added to the Trickster card pool.
-  Prepared strike was reduced to common
-  Cover Your Tracks is now epic and has been redesigned
-  Runescarred Den was moved to common
-  Friends in High Places had the energy cost removed and was made epic
-  We kissed Kiss of Death goodbye when we removed it from the card pool

That's it for now.  We hope you enjoy this update.  We believe that this will open up the design space for even more builds and interesting enemy designs.  We can't want to see what builds you come up with!
With love from the Nevergreen Team,
Your friendly neighborhood programmer, Reggi

notes.title: Dec 18th update
notes.notes:
Legacy upgrade cards inherit the speed of the base legacy card.
Trickster 7 state applies to Legacy, Companion, and multiclass cards.
Fixed bug with Ravenous Steward fight not starting.
Fixed bug where some normal nodes had elite enemies.
Adjusted fight rewards.  Certain rewards like swaps and splits will not appear until later in the run.

notes.title: Lucky Update
notes.notes:
That's right, another update today!  In line with the previous update, we are trying to make the game more fair.  This update addresses concerns about class abilities.  We wanted to make playing the Trickster more fair, so we decided to change the Trickster's ability, Lucky 7.  Now, the 7 state will only effect Trickster cards, or cards override by the Trickster's abilities.  This means that being at 7 will not double effects from enemy cards, curse cards, legacy cards, or multiclass cards.  7s are just for the Trickster.  We hope that this change makes playing the Trickster more fun, and most importantly, more fair.
Also, we changed some other cards with fairness in mind.

- Heavy Swing values were cut in half.
- Bludgeon is now slow.
- Bloated Boa enemy was completely redesigned.
- Fire Breath costs more to keep at level one, but is cheaper to downgrade.
- One with Aether was completely changed

Also fixed a minor issue with the Archive view not being scrollable on some screen resolutions.

Hopefully, this is another step in the right direction.  We look forward to hearing your feedback on this update!
- Reggi, your friendly neighborhood programmer

notes.title: Enemy Intent Patch
notes.notes:
Our intention from the inception of Mori Carta is to make a deckbuilding game that is tough but fair to the player.  We are constantly listening to our players to gauge how fair the game is, and we understand that there are many times in which the RNG feels unfair.  We are taking steps to fix this so runs don't end simply with a bad roll.  This update is the first step in a series of updates we intend to roll out over the coming months.  We hope that this and the following updates will move the game in the direction of being more fair to the player.

This update may seem small, but it should give the player a key piece of information to make strategic decisions.
-When the next card is an enemy card, the card back on the deck at the bottom will show the enemy card back, so players will know that the next card is an enemy card.

Additional updates
-Fixed an issue with localization.  Only English should be available now.
-Made Crash, Wreck, and Roil slow.  (These mostly appear for the water enemy cards in the prologue.  This should make this section of the prologue more predictable.)

Thank you for your patience and feedback.  We hope to make Mori Carta as fair and fun as possible, and we couldn't do it without your help.
-Reggi, your friendly neighborhood programmer

notes.title: Event Map Update
notes.notes:
Hey there!

Hoo boy. Today’s patch is a big one. I think I said that last patch, too. But trust me it’s a figurative ton of the good good. So many great things for all our Mori Cartians out there to sink their teeth into. We talked with players, read your comments and made some pretty significant changes that we think will enhance the experience of the hottest handless roguelike deckbuilder out there.

Let’s hit the big points first. The flow of the game has been re-imagined and streamlined! No longer will you move between Companion runs and Wild runs in an effort to unlock “The Long Walk.” It has all been condensed into a single run format. Now when you want to try to make a one turn kill Nova Scholar deck, you can test your swiping skills against a spectrum of enemies as you explore our new Run Map! We wanted to give players a bit more choice in what kind of run they have, and landed on a roguelike classic. How many elites can you fight in one run? And what are those purple rings?!

Companions have also been rolled into the game’s core loop. Now when you play a run you will have a chance for companions to show up along the path. And certain companions can be combined, meaning that you can have more than one companion adding value to your deck! Who knows? Maybe Bran and Poppet could really hit it off! You will still need to help the companion before they join you on the rest of your journey, and you may need to help them more than once. Some companions are just needy like that.

The list of improvements, changes, and added features is long so let’s get a bit more succinct as we move through them:

Editing your deck has never been easier with adjustments to 
Swaps and Augments.
As well as new options in the Split and 
Cursed Offerings. What does that mean?! Play and find out!
Various improvements to UI can be observed throughout the game. Highlights including the Character Select Screen and a new End Run Screen! We would LOVE to see captures of your end run screens to see all the wild decks you are winning or losing with!
ART! There’s more of it! And it’s even prettier than before, if I just humble brag for a bit there, thanks. But it’s not just card art, we also added VFX to in several places. Hover states in combat, glowing on the Might and Resilience to show when it’s active. Check it out!
Special mention as well to our new promotional art featured above! Dominick Domingo was kind enough to lend us his talents to really bring Hau, the Spirit of Change and Death to life. Thanks Nick!
Legacy cards, or the exhaust cards that you start a run with, have an added feature. They can now be upgraded if you beat the correlating Echo on your run! Let’s see if this shakes up the Legacy meta.
Quick Mode! Sometimes it can be a bit much to swipe all of the cards in your deck. Here’s to you Paw of the South! We wanted to alleviate this as an option for some of our more veteran players. There are now Options in the Setting for different skips to accelerate your play of Mori Carta. 
A new title music track! We are working with Neil Quillen, a game composer, on some great new music and here’s the first track! It’s not complete yet, but we thought it was so cool we wanted to get you an early taste. Look forward to more!

What caught your eye the most? I am still trying to make the perfect OTK Nova deck. And we want to make sure that you can do cool stuff with all of the classes! So let’s talk a bit about each of them:

Scholar:
Scholar is the starting experience for every player and so it has received a lot of love from the team. We looked at the balance of Scholar cards as it pertains to rarity and moved some things around. Take a look at epics and rares to see what’s new!

Trickster:
Trickster is always walking the tightrope, and we love that about her game play! But some cards were a little bit too on the razor’s edge so we eased their balance. One highlight is increasing the power of the Seven Cards. We want to celebrate activating the more challenging cards in Trickster.

Druid:
The Druid was struggling. Our internal data was showing that our environmental friend was getting beat up by the dangerous foes in Mori Carta. She lost runs at a higher rate than the other classes by a decent margin. So we buffed Druids starting cards. This will help with energy problems, and we expect, bring the Druid in line with the other archetypes.

Atoned:
One of the highlights for Atoned is Initiates. They were a bit of a problem on the Atoned. While they were decently balanced in their power, they could quickly clog up your deck and just take a long time to swipe through, which created a bad feeling for the player. We removed one step in the upgrade chain to make them more impactful earlier in fights. We compensated for this increase in power by reducing the overall number of initiates that get added by other cards.

And that’s… the patch? It feels like I must have missed something because there are so many things that went into the game since we last pushed a change. Thank you for your continued support of Mori Carta. We love seeing comments, reviews, or content that you guys create. We always look forward to talking with any Mori Cartians.

So keep talking with us! Let us know what you think about the changes so that we can be ready for our March 1.0 release. 

Keep gaming,
Seth “SingingSwordsman” Cornwall and the Nevergreen Games Team

notes.title: Enemy Art Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! 

Happy Friday! We’re coming at you with the content we promised! Biggest feature this week is art! Get excited to see the new faces of the denizens of Mori Carta because… *drum roll*

All enemies have art for their portraits! 

There is additionally a slew of fixes and of course: a balance pass! We noticed in the numbers that some fights were just brutal. Some of the enemies were just slapping everyone around too much. So we have redesigned some of their fights to be more balanced, and on the whole more interesting!

The druid was also struggling a lot in the numbers, so they got a little more love then the rest. But let’s get a list going!

Scholar:
Source: Cut. Moved to Druid.

Trickster:
Cloak Of Shadows:
It was a bit expensive, 6 -> 4 energy. The material on the cloak isn’t that pricey.
Punchline:
7 -> 5 damage. The jokes were too good, everyone was always laughing too hard. 

Druid:
Blood Rage:
Damage on the left is brought down from 4 -> 2. Bit too easy to slap fools with the free side, and set up some of the stronger but more risky left side damage resonates. 
Claw:
Gain 1 energy added on the left.
Pay 1 -> 2 energy on the right and 3 -> 4 Damage.
Claw wasn’t competing with the other classes' damage cards. So we got him a mani-pedi.
Shaking Earth: 
Druid can really struggle when they have no energy, so this card can exacerbate some of the challenges the class faces. It will still cost x, but resonating it will bring you up to 3 energy afterwards, which is good!
Wax & Wane: Moved over from Source on Scholar. Now alternates between sides on upgrade/downgrade. We think this fits well in the Druid, and will help with some of their energy problem

Atoned:
Aesceticism -> Asceticisim. Love those typos.

Enemy Cards:
Threaten:
This occurs across a couple fights, but we were seeing some classes struggle, so we flipped the sides to ease that tension. No other change.
Crushing Descent:
Similarly to Threaten, the orientation of this card was affecting the challenge of this card. So we flipped it.

Enemies:
Armed Echo:
His arms were a bit too much for some classes, and he did the same thing over and over. Now you can slightly block his plethora of marring arms.
Avaricious Banker:
New fight alert! This banker will take you for all your worth!
Caged Captain:
Mr. Captain is now in a Cage! You can choose to let him out. Or fight him inside his cage, which is a little harder to do. Your choice!
Deepwood Shaman:
The elements are a little more durable in this fight, with some increases to energy costs across the board.
Doomed Flock:
A slight number buff on Blood Sacrifice from 7 -> 8 and it’s now slow. The number of sheep has increased and it will take longer to wrangle them. And sadly it will be more painful! :(
Entrenched Swarm:
This guy didn’t have enough nests. Let’s give him a nest for every nest he has.
Grounded Echo:
This fight was a bit overtuned and just kind of a slugfest. Now you can go “blow for blow” and one of you will come out on top a bit faster!
Grudge Echo:
You can now embrace his grudge, leaning into his hatred of you to make it easier to defeat him. His hatred will make you mightier!
Headless Giant:
The second turn, Fall, now has a reshuffle on it. A headless target was a bit too easy to handle for all you pro gamers.
Lycanthrope:
Mori Carta’s resident werewolf wasn’t very threatening. Now he’ll be a bit more so.
Mistveil Current:
We wanted to push the power of River of Sin to the front, so that you have to push through the might and the resilience together!
Phase Swarm:
This fight was a little monotonous, so we added some spice by putting a reshuffle on Underwhelm! Now you won’t know when you’re going to be sent back to the top to be truly overwhelmed by dreadlings!
Pied Piper:
We’re always forgetting about this fight and its challenges, but through sheer happenstance the Piper’s flute got tuned. It should be a little less grating to the ears.
Raiders:
These guys were getting trounced by the scholar. But they learned to not listen anymore. Ignorance is bliss, and makes beating scholars easy. 
Smiling Echo:
His disturbing smile is now cursed as well! But if you jump into the deep end, you might come out the other side unscathed.
The Hulks:
There is a pod of hulks that are all rivals with each other. But they all agreed that they should work on themselves a bit more, so now they are a bit tougher. Where they would have added just one card they now add two. 

Companions:
Bran:
Bran’s tasty, tasty trail rations are now, in fact, delectable and will heal more.
Ker:
We wanted to send a little love to our resident Doctor. Players should feel a bit healthier while helping Ker out.

And that's the patch! Thanks for playing Mori Carta! If you haven't yet, tell all your friends about the steam Steam Strategy Fest sale that's going on right now!

Until next time,
The Nevergreen Team

notes.title: Lore Update Patch
notes.notes:
Greeting and salutations everyone!

We’re back with a patch! Hooray for content! Today we’re going to be adding in a large batch of flavor text for the cards! The team has had many a conversation about “What happened to the Fool after the prologue?” or “What exactly does the Atoned have ‘Faith’ in?” And we want to encourage our players to share in the story of Mori Carta. 

Our goal with this patch is to lay the groundwork for some lore and get it in front you. As we are in Early Access we are always growing the game in new and exciting ways to put the best game on your computer. But we can’t water all these growing opportunities alone, for them to bear fruit we ask the community “how are we doing?”

You will notice that we attempted to continue with our idea that all text is written in a variety of poetic styles. Which ones make you laugh? Which ones make you sad? Which ones make you wonder? We don’t expect each of the poems to be a home run but we hope that they will add that extra bit of flavor for those who like that taste. 

The flavor texts will help set the tone for the story of Mori Carta going forward, so expect to see more down the road. We want to give more definition to the companion quests, so that a player will understand why they’re hanging out with Poppet. We want to explore more about the 4 (soon to be 5) classes, as well as the Fool. So this is not the end!

Thank you for checking out Mori Carta, and for reading this post. 

Until next time!
Seth “SingingSwordsman” Cornwall & The Nevergreen Team

P.S. We did the thing! We talked again, and so soon! Huzzah!

notes.title: Update 0.2.4
notes.notes:
Path 0.2.4

Hey there Mori Cartians!

SingingSwordsman and the Nevergreen Games team here, back with some bright and fresh changes to your new favorite deck builder. We wound up accumulating quite a few awesome changes to the balance, design, and look of Mori Carta and there’s a lot to be excited about.

I do want to take a minute at the start here to apologize to you, the community. The live build that was available before this patch brought changes to the way rewards are given to the player. While we believe in the overall design of the change, the balance and implementation of these rewards were not ok. Players were receiving greatly diminished returns, resulting in weaker decks and a considerably more punishing experience. We are very sorry for this error, and for how long it took us to fix this. 

We have adjusted the reward levels to be just right. Not too little or too much, but just right… we hope! Of course we will keep an eye on community feedback and our own internal testing to make sure we get this right. Because rewards are what is fun about deck builders, you are trying to build a deck after all!

Let’s go through all the changes. Here’s the patch notes:

Design:	

 Might and Resilience both had their functionality changed. Now they will tick down every time they are used. Notably, this changes the interactivity with “on Swipe” and “Trigger” effects so that might will not be applied on play, instead it will be added on swipe and then reduced by one. These changes were put in as a balancing factor. We were constantly torn between the varying levels of might and resilience. This will allow us to be a little bit more generous with them and we will be keeping an eye on its balance moving forward.
 The reward flow has been rearranged. The player will be asked what reward they wish to receive before fighting an enemy, and then receive that reward upon defeating them. When the reward is offered you can sometimes choose to fight an elite for greater rewards.
 Elite and Boss fights are indicated on the reward selection screen. Elite cards have a silver card back and bosses a gold card back.
 New reward options in the “Defensive” and “Offensive” shops.
 The echo enemies have been changed to elite status from normal.


Art:

 We mentioned the enemy card backs above, but there’s also one for normal enemies with a cool little monster guy. There are also new card backs for each of the classes! Which one is your favorite?
 An animation was added when your block is reduced to zero.
 The position of the Dodge and Faith counters, for Trickster and Atoned respectively, have been moved above the card wells. Similar to the Druid’s resonate tracker.
 Elite enemies, as well as cards marked with a gold gemstone, have had their trim upgraded to a new shiny and scary appearance to show how mean they really are.
 Wind Devil and Court of Storms have had their art updated.


Card Balance

Legacy:

 A Smile (and “A Grimace” on the Smiling Echo) was nerfed to from 4 -> 3 damage


Scholar:

 Dancing Flames was removed from the pool


Trickster:

 Ace of Sovereignty was added at the epic level
 Big Bag had its energy cost reduce from 10 -> 7 and the number of Blades added from 15 -> 10
 Blade Flurry was changed: pay 4 to gain a on swipe right trigger that adds a blade
 Arrows has been changed to add 1 discard on the left side
 Lunge was removed from the pool
 Alchemist had it effect on the left changed to add a Elixir on exhaust, and the right side now costs 5 energy


Druid:

 Cairn Clearing was changed to add two Mother’s Protection for 2 energy, but then downgrades to Carve Into Stone which upgrade back up into Cairn Clearing for 3 energy. Clever players may want to consider the implications of this change.
 Ravage was changed in a similar fashion
 Tribal Rite was added to the pool
 Cracked Horn was removed from the pool
 Mursa the Cub was added to the pool
 Rich Soil was removed from the pool
 Mother’s Embrace had its sides flipped so that the add card is now on the right side
 Wolf Pack had its sides flipped so that the add card is now on the right side and the might is on the left side
 Allstone origination has its sides flipped so that 3 Allstones are added on the right side and 1 Nullstone is added on the left side
 Overgrowth has its left side changed to blank 
 Equilibrium was changed to be a one time trigger effect that heals and adds a Conflict on deal damage
 Druid’s Garb was added to the epic pool
 Reciprocity was removed from the Druid and added to the Possessed


Atoned:

 Sanctify was removed
 Added Prophetic Prediction
 Added Prophetic Pyre
 Added Renounce
 Divine Decisions had its add card adjusted:
 Divine Bolt exhaust on the left, faith based damage on the right
 Divine Deflection, faith based block on the left, exhaust on the right
 Exculpatory Tale’s had its add card adjusted:
 Divine Barrier, exhaust on the left, faith based block on the right
 Entropic Dissolution, 4 block on the left, exhaust on the right
 Cautionary Tale had its add card adjusted:
 Divine Bolt, exhaust on the left, faith based damage on the right
 Entropic Burn, 4 damage on the left, exhaust on the right
 Entropic Offering had its add card adjusted:
 Remove All Doubt, exhaust on the left, pay X for X block on the right
 Remove All Doubters, pay X for X damage on the left, exhaust on the right 
 Thirst had its add cards adjusted:
 Slake, gain 4 energy on the left, exhaust on the right
 Aesecticism, exhaust on the left, pay X to gain energy equal to faith on the right
 Shield of the Redeemed had its energy cost increased from 2 -> 3
 Emberwing’s Aid had its energy cost increased from 2 -> 5
 Sinner’s Bonds had its rarity increased to rare
 Ascension had its energy costs changed to 3 -> 5 -> 7
 Empower was changed to add a wheel of faith based damage or armor on the left, and cost 8 on the right
 Conflagration had its energy cost was increased from 4 -> 5
 Cower was adjusted to break your block, effectively setting your block to 15
 Talon’s Thrum was renamed to Fists of Faith
 Fists of Faith was renamed to Crusader’s Strike
 Midnight Commune was redesigned as an Epic card that adds Initiates on Exhaust
 Call and Response was changed to 6 damage on both sides
 Fickle Flight was change to 6 block on both sides
 Assign Identity had its rarity increased to rare
 Retribution was removed from the game
 Reckoning was changed to deal faith wound instead of adding a Retribution
 The Pawned Trinket chain now deals faith wound on the right instead of adding a retribution
 Day III now deals faith based wound instead of adding a Retribution
 Vindicated Violence was removed from the pool
 Build the Temple was changed to 2 block on swipe and 2 wound on swipe permanent from 1 respectively
 Denial was moved to rare
 Prophetic Pyre had exhaust added to the right side
 Convergent Affirmation had its name changes to Convergent Affinity
 Convergent Denial had its name changes to Convergent Affirmation


Woof. That’s a change list. And we are excited for the changes this will bring! Let us know here on Steam or on our Discord. We’d love to hear from you! 

Once again we apologize for the delay in response to an unfortunate play state. Thanks for reading and we’ll talk to you soon!

Cheers,
The Nevergreen Games Team

notes.title: Patch 0.2.0 & Sale
notes.notes:
Greetings from the team at Nevergreen Games! 

Mori Carta has been live for a little over a month and we are so happy to have seen so many people check out our Early Access release. The path before us is an exciting one full of improvements, updates, and fun! Thanks for choosing to support Mori Carta.

With that said, our first major update is live! We have seen several small updates, but this is our first large step forward towards release. Check out the patch notes here. 

Some noteworthy highlights include:

-A new playable class, the Atoned! Their main mechanic Faith allows them to scale their power up throughout a fight. But the higher your faith, the more challenging it becomes to maintain. We're excited for people to try out this unique and challenging class.
-A new companion run, "Rael, He Who Grapples." Battle physical manifestations of the seven deadly sins. Each with their own way to wreak havoc on you and Rael. 
-Reward changes! The system for dispensing rewards to the player in runs has been changed for the better! Players should feel a difference in how they build their deck, with new options being presented.
-Limited keyboard and controller support. Full functionality is planned for down the road, but we thought that these changes felt great when playing and wanted to share them with you. Effectively, the functionality works within the combat screen and shop, but not on the main menu or character select screen. We'll bring that later on.

Mori Carta is on sale! For those who haven’t had a chance to pick up Mori Carta yet, now is the time! Tell a friend about it, heck buy them a copy! Spread the word about the newest handless deck building roguelike on the market!

The road ahead for Early Access is bright, with new things just around the corner. We are committed to bringing the best experience we can to your hands. There will be a follow up rewards system patch to bring our vision of the system to the player. After that, the next major update will focused on updating the UI.
 
Feedback is encouraged and desired, whether it’s here on Steam, on our Discord, or through some other means. Please reach out! We love engaging with those who have chosen to join around Mori Carta, and hope that many more will embrace it as a unique edition to the roguelike deck builder genre. 

Best,
Nevergreen Games

notes.title: Update 0.2.0
notes.notes:
This is a major content update starting with a new playable archetype, The Atoned.  The Atoned uses Faith, which allows them to scale their power through a fight. But the higher your faith, the more challenging it becomes to maintain. We're excited for people to try this unique and challenging archetype.

Additionally, we are introducing a new companion: Rael, He Who Grapples
Battle physical manifestations of the seven deadly sins in Rael's run.  

Additional Updates:

 Reward cards have been improved and will now offer better and more interesting choices based on how far the player has progressed in their run.  
 Added limited keyboard and joystick controls.  Combat, shop, and event cards can now be navigated using a joystick or the arrow keys.  Full controls for menu navigation will be coming soon.
 Some sound effects were updated.
 The event and character select screen backgrounds were updated.
 The initial tutorial cards had their artwork updated.
 Removed the card Time's Ebb from the enemy Dream Catcher and replaced with Fate's Pet
